title: Control Plane: Customer Comms Scenarios for Regulated Deployments
summary: Working set of short, persona-specific messaging and ready-to-run scripts for early sales and solution-engineering conversations about Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) with regulated customers. Purpose: reduce friction in first 3 calls, map common risk frames to concrete controls we can commit to, and define when to loop in SRE/product or legal for escalations.
elevator_pitch: For teams with regulated data needs, Redwood Private provides a customer-controlled control plane plus an optional on-prem inference package that preserves developer ergonomics while meeting auditability, key-management, and network isolation requirements. We minimize vendor exposure without sacrificing model performance or rollout velocity.
mid_level_message: Start with the risk frame the buyer cares about (data residency, auditability, separation of duties). Then show the bundle of controls: private control plane (customer-managed), optional on-prem inference nodes, KMS/HSM integration, retained telemetry that can be tuned, and explicit audit log retention policies. Emphasize that the API and SDK remain the same developers use in hosted mode, reducing integration risk.
deep_technical_message: Implementation notes to share with platform/security teams: the control plane endpoints are hosted in a customer-specific VPC peering model or deployed as an air-gapped control plane. Control plane only stores non-sensitive metadata by default; model weights and inference compute can be confined to customer-managed hosts. Keys are never exported from customer KMS; we support cloud KMS and customer HSMs. Audit logs are delivered to the customer's log sink (S3/GCS/Azure) and include request IDs, model version, route, latency, and config diffs. We support formal pen tests and can produce architecture diagrams and threat models on request.
objections_and_rebuttals: Objection: "Customer is concerned the control plane will have access to PII and sensitive prompts." Rebuttal: "Control plane stores routing/config metadata, not plaintext prompts by default. Customer can opt-out of telemetry forwarding and configure prefix/KV caching to stay on customer hosts. For high-sensitivity workloads we recommend on-prem inference nodes; in that mode the control plane never sees inputs/outputs unless explicitly routed for diagnostics."

Objection: "We can't allow vendor-managed keys or secret exposure." Rebuttal: "We integrate with customer KMS/HSM; keys never leave your key vault. If needed we support HSM-based signing and bring-your-own-key policies tied to role-based access control and hardware-backed attestations."

Objection: "How do you support audit/regulatory requests (e.g., GDPR deletion, SOC2 evidence)?" Rebuttal: "We provide configurable log retention policies, deletion hooks for stored metadata, and packaged evidence bundles for SOC2/ISO requests. For Private customers we can run controlled extractions into their audit storage and support on-site audits by approved auditors under NDA."

Objection: "We need strict network isolation and no egress to vendor services." Rebuttal: "Private offers both VPC peering and full on-prem bundles. With on-prem, control plane can be deployed within customer network and inference compute never touches public internet. We document required endpoints and provide an allowlist for minimal admin operations."

Objection: "We're worried about vendor lock-in and model drift control." Rebuttal: "Customers can pin model versions and we support model artifacts export. For on-prem deployments, runbooks and upgrade automation are provided so customers control upgrade cadence; our rollouts support canary patterns and rollbacks to protect from regressions."

Objection: "Competitors claim they have a simpler legal posture because everything is self-hosted." Rebuttal: "Self-hosted isn't the whole story: we offer a hybrid that combines self-hosted inference with a controlled, minimal control plane and clear, contractual commitments (SLA, incident response, audit rights). That reduces operational burden while meeting legal requirements. Provide checklist comparing operational overhead vs total cost of ownership."

Objection: "We need encryption in transit and at rest with verifiable attestations." Rebuttal: "All traffic uses TLS 1.3 with mutual auth for private endpoints. For at-rest we support customer-managed keys. For high-assurance environments we provide attestations and integration with remote attestation solutions (e.g., Nitro Enclaves / SGX workflows) as a professional-services engagement."

Objection: "What happens during incident response — can you provide runbooks and SLAs?" Rebuttal: "Yes. For Dedicated and Private customers we provide SLA-backed response windows, a pre-shared incident communications plan, runbooks for RTO/RPO expectations, and a named technical account contact for escalations. We can include required SLAs into contract language where needed."
competitive_notes: Major cloud provider endpoints: strong on global infrastructure and compliance baselines, but often require customers to assemble multiple services (KMS, logging, VPC peering) themselves for comparable auditability; pricing and latency profiles vary by region.

Open inference runtimes: attractive for control but require heavy ops investment to maintain patching, autoscaling, and performant batching; Redwood differentiates by shipping an ops-light on-prem option and clear upgrade/rollout tooling.

Inference vendors with air-gap solutions: some offer air-gapped inference but still lack developer ergonomics (SDK parity, streaming, function-calling). Emphasize parity with hosted API to reduce migration friction.

Startups selling purely on self-hosted: can be cheaper short-term but lack SLA, monitoring, and a path to scale; highlight our Dedicated to Private ramp path and ability to move workloads between modes.

Key competitive positioning: we are the pragmatic middle path — preserve developer experience, offer legally-aligned controls, and minimize ops cost for regulated buyers while providing contractual assurances.
scripts: Initial outreach email (procurement): 'Hi <Name>, quick note — Redwood has a Private offering tailored for regulated workloads that preserves developer APIs while enabling customer-managed control planes and KMS integration. Would love to schedule a short 20-minute call to map your compliance posture and show a targeted architecture diagram.'

Security-first call opener: 'Can you walk me through your worst-case data exposure scenario? I'd like to understand what you need from a control plane vs inference nodes so we can align the minimal surface area you want Redwood to touch.'

Platform-level demo script: 'Show console with per-route metrics, audit log export settings, a sample KMS integration flow, and how to pin a model version and rollback. Then toggle telemetry forwarding off to demonstrate zero-exfiltration mode.'

Legal checklist email: 'Attached is a 1-page summary of controls we commit to for Private customers: KMS integrations, audit logs to customer sinks, contractual deletion hooks, pen test schedule, and on-site audit support. Let us know which items need tweaks and we'll route to legal.'
decision_triggers: Any explicit requirement for customer-managed KMS/HSM -> escalate to Solutions Engineering for architecture and SRE for attestations.
Request for on-site/on-prem packaging or air-gapped deployment -> loop in Product and Professional Services to scope effort and timeline.
Audit or regulatory request requiring custom evidence bundles or auditor access -> involve Legal and Compliance to draft contract language and NDA for auditor access.
If the buyer asks for SLA changes or bespoke incident response terms -> escalate to GTM leadership and finance for commercial negotiation.
If buyer requests remote attestation or hardware enclave support -> route to Applied ML and Infrastructure for feasibility and timeline.
If buyer expresses desire to avoid all vendor-managed components -> capture as a PS scope item and present tradeoffs in TCO comparison.
If procurement insists on exported model artifacts and rollback guarantees -> capture as technical acceptance criteria for the onboarding SOW.
key_metrics_and_controls: SLA: configurable latency and availability SLAs for Dedicated/Private customers with named response windows.
Audit logs: per-request metadata delivered to customer sink; retention configurable (30/90/365 days or custom).
KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys, support for cloud KMS and validated HSM integrations.
Network isolation: VPC peering, private endpoints, and fully on-prem inference packaging available.
Telemetry controls: toggles for telemetry forwarding, sampling rates, and opt-outs for request content.
Model governance: model pinning, version auditing, rollout canaries, auto-fallback policies.
Pen tests & compliance: scheduled penetration tests, compliance evidence bundles, support for on-site audits under NDA.
legal_clauses_to_offer: Data residency clause: commit to keeping persisted data in customer-controlled storage in agreed regions.
KMS / key ownership: BYOK clause stating keys remain under customer control and never exported by vendor.
Audit rights: scoped auditor access under NDA and agreed operational windows.
Breach notification: contracted timeline for incident notification and scope of disclosure aligned with customer requirements.
Service credits & SLAs: tiered credits tied to availability/latency breaches for Dedicated/Private customers.
next_steps: 1) Run a 20-minute rehearsal with SE/Sales to practice the security-first opener (target: within 5 business days).
2) Draft a 1-page architecture snapshot template to attach to discovery emails (owner: SE team).
3) Create a redlined legal starter pack for regulated buyers with pre-approved clauses (owner: Legal).
4) Build a checklist for Solution Engineering that maps buyer sentences to decision_triggers and required internal approvers.
5) Schedule an internal review with Applied ML to confirm attestation capabilities and a supported timeline for hardware enclave projects.
